reason: Visible candidate bottleneck: both 512-step K loops issue two pointer increments plus a countdown decrement and branch on every iteration. That makes K-loop scheduling and reuse experiments the strongest initial hypotheses; the instruction sequence alone does not establish a timing cause. Next are loop-control and stack-scratch changes with narrower scope. Traversal, layout, packing, and fallback-tail proposals carry broader locality or correctness risks. Historical scores are noisy and lack paired controls, so they do not distinguish these proposals. All expected gains are unverified.
